question.worked_solution:
First, we let

$$
L={lim}_{x\to \pi /4}\,\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}}{x-\frac{\pi }{4}}.
$$

Comparing this with the formula for the instantaneous rate of change

$$
{f}^{′}(a)={lim}_{x\to a}\frac{f(x)-f(a)}{x-a},
$$

we see that if we let $f(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)$ and $a=\frac{\pi }{4}$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}\,(\frac{\pi }{4}) & ={lim}_{x\to \pi /4}\frac{f(x)-f\,(\frac{\pi }{4})}{x-\frac{\pi }{4}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \pi /4}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)-cos\,(\frac{\pi }{4})}{x-\frac{\pi }{4}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \pi /4}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}}{x-\frac{\pi }{4}}=L.\end{aligned}
$$

 

This confirms that $L={f}^{′}\,(\frac{\pi }{4}).$

Computing the derivative, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=-\operatorname{sin}⁡(x),\,{f}^{′}\,(\frac{\pi }{4})=-sin\,(\frac{\pi }{4})=-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},
$$

and therefore, we conclude that $L=-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.$
